results.input: What's the difference between a fixed rate and a floating rate home loan package?
results.response:
**Fixed rate:** The interest rate stays the same for a set period, so you're protected if rates rise and monthly budgeting is easier. Early redemption during that period often carries charges. If market rates fall during the fixed period, you may end up paying a comparatively higher rate. [7] Once the fixed period ends, the rate becomes a floating rate, and on the DBS Private Home Loan you can switch to another package for free at that point. [5]

**Floating (variable) rate:** The interest rate can change periodically, often in relation to a reference rate, so your payments may go up or down when that rate changes. [7] Examples of reference rates include SORA and rates offered by the CPF Board. [7] DBS's floating packages are based on SORA or the Fixed Deposit Home Rate (FHR). [5]

- **3M SORA** is based on overnight interbank borrowing rates, and it is published daily on the MAS website at 9am. [10]
- **FHR** is pegged to DBS's own fixed deposit rate, and changes are at the bank's discretion in response to market conditions. [7][10]

DBS also offers an Easy Switch Loan for completed properties. It starts with a fixed rate, and you can switch to a 3M SORA package any time after disbursement. [5]

For current package rates, DBS asks customers to contact them, as rates aren't listed on the Private Property page. [5] A DBS banker can walk you through the details.

results.input: Is there a cap on how much unsecured credit I can have across all banks?
results.response:
Yes. There is an industry-wide borrowing limit on credit card, charge card and unsecured balances, added up across all financial institutions in Singapore. It is meant to help people avoid building up excessive unsecured debt [1].

**The limit:** It is a multiple of your monthly income. It started at 24 times from 1 June 2015, was lowered to 18 times from 1 June 2017, and has been 12 times since 1 June 2019 [1][2].

**How it's worked out:** Your aggregate interest-bearing unsecured outstanding balance across all institutions is divided by your monthly income [2].

**Exceptions:** The limit doesn't apply to unsecured loans for education, business and medical purposes [1].

**If you go over it for 3 consecutive months (per DBS's records),** DBS will not allow you to:
- charge new amounts to your existing cards or use unsecured facilities issued by DBS,
- get new cards or unsecured facilities from DBS, or
- get credit limit increases on existing cards or unsecured facilities from DBS [2].

There is no set time limit to bring your balances down. Once you are below the limit, you can ask DBS to review your credit situation. Your payment obligations continue in the meantime [6]. If you need help with repayment options, you can approach DBS or Credit Counselling Singapore at 6225 5227 [6].

These figures are as published on the DBS page as of 27 Oct 2026.

**What TDSR is**

TDSR (Total Debt Servicing Ratio) is the portion of your gross monthly income that goes towards repaying all your monthly debt obligations, including the home loan you're applying for [2]. The rule says your TDSR should be no more than 55% [2][5].

**Why it matters for your home loan**

- **It caps how much you can borrow.** Banks look at your debt against your income when working out your maximum home loan amount [4]. If your TDSR is above 55%, the loan amount has to be reduced [10].
- **Your existing debts count.** For example, if your existing monthly debt obligations are 10% of your monthly income, the maximum property loan would be based on the remaining 45% of your monthly income [1].
- **It applies to property loans generally.** Banks must calculate TDSR for any loan to purchase a property, any loan secured by a property, and refinancing of these loans [7].
- **Repayments are calculated conservatively.** Banks must work out your monthly property loan instalments using the higher of the medium-term interest rate floor and the thereafter interest rate [10].

**If you're buying an HDB flat**

There is a second limit, the Mortgage Servicing Ratio (MSR). No more than 30% of your gross monthly income should go towards all your property loans, including the new one. It applies to HDB flats and certain executive condominiums [6][9].

I can explain how revolving loans or existing property loans are treated in the calculation if that would help. For a figure based on your own income and commitments, the DBS mortgage calculator or a banker can help [4].
